clue.text: Judge and arbitrator in change of scene

blocks.note: J is the standard abbreviation for judge
short for umpire, the arbitrator in a game

explanation.surface: A judge and a mediator are sent off somewhere new to hear a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In film, a jump (as in a jump cut) is an abrupt cut from one shot or setting to another.

clue.text: Lady upset about corruption bringing Independent in smartly

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so the letters of Lady are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the rearranged lady wraps around the next piece
bringing one thing in puts it inside another, here inside the word for corruption

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
rot is moral decay or corruption
I is the usual abbreviation for Independent

explanation.surface: A lady is distressed that corruption has crept into the Independent newspaper, the paper this puzzle appears in.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged lady splits in two, wrapping around the corruption word, which in turn takes in the newspaper's initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroitly means with skill and dexterity, which is one sense of doing something smartly.

clue.text: Exotic wood featured in Cakes And Ale

indicators.note: something featured in a title appears inside it, so the answer sits within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of Cakes, all of And and the start of Ale

explanation.surface: Some exotic timber gets a mention in Somerset Maugham's novel Cakes and Ale.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital letters make it look like a quotation from the book title; they hide the join between the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandal is the old name for the fragrant East Indian sandalwood tree and its timber, imported from abroad.

clue.text: Scold furiously, but not irate, surprisingly

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is an unexpected arrangement, so these letters come out in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gives a furious telling-off while oddly claiming not to be angry at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface contradiction is the joke: the calm words are themselves the angry phrase rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear into someone is an idiom for attacking them verbally, berating them with great vigour.

clue.text: Company holding a function in gambling venue

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so the company's abbreviation wraps around what follows

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
taken as written
sin, short for sine, is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A firm holds a corporate function at a casino.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' looks like a party, but it is the mathematical sine, written SIN. C(A SIN)O.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a building where people go to play games of chance for money.

clue.text: Cut of meat excellent in Paris - cordon bleu?

blocks.note: a rib is a cut of beef or pork
bon is French for good

explanation.surface: A cut of meat, excellent in a Parisian restaurant, ought to be cordon bleu cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: Cordon bleu suggests top-class cookery, matching the meat, but literally it is French for 'blue ribbon', the sash of an order of knighthood; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordon bleu is literally a blue sash worn as a decoration, one particular kind of the answer.

clue.text: Almost frozen stream perhaps showing eventual strong response

blocks.note: something almost frozen has nearly stopped moving, so it is very slow
burn is Scottish and northern English for a stream; 'perhaps' marks it as one example

explanation.surface: A nearly iced-over brook is offered as a picture of a strong reaction that builds up over time.
explanation.walkthrough: BURN is the Scots word for a small stream or brook.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow burn is an idiom for anger or emotion that builds gradually before becoming intense.

clue.text: Pound head of goon in repeated violent TV show

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of goon is used
in places the preceding pieces inside the word for repeated

blocks.note: quid is British slang for a pound sterling
its first letter
something repeated is the same as before

explanation.surface: A thug gets pummelled over and over in a brutal television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' reads as a verb for hitting, but it is British slang for the money; both it and the goon's initial go inside the word for repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Squid Game is the South Korean television drama in which contestants are killed for losing children's games.

clue.text: 17 tossed my boxes into second Loch

indicators.note: tossed things are thrown about, so the letters of my boxes land in a new order
into places the rearranged words between the two single letters that follow

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
taken as written, to be rearranged
L is the map abbreviation for loch

explanation.surface: A famous seducer throws his boxes into a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is the answer to 17 down, CASANOVA. 'Loch' looks like a place, but it only gives its L, with S at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Casanova, the legendary seducer, is held up as an example of someone thought sexually irresistible.

clue.text: After reflection, Star Wars character accommodating right Shakespearean spirit

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is back to front, so the character's name is read backwards
accommodating means giving room to, so the reversed name holds the next letter inside

blocks.note: Princess Leia of the Star Wars films
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A Star Wars figure, on reflection, makes room for a ghostly character from Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the airy sprite who serves Prospero in Shakespeare's play The Tempest.

clue.text: Returned pictures I found in brickie's carrier depicting a sword

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective meaning sword-shaped

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word for pictures is read backwards
a thing found in another sits inside it, so the letter goes into the carrier

blocks.note: pix is informal shorthand for pictures
a hod is the trough on a pole a bricklayer uses to carry bricks
taken as written

explanation.surface: Photographs come back showing a sword hidden in a builder's hod.
explanation.walkthrough: A brickie is a bricklayer; XIP + HO(I)D.
explanation.definitionFit: Xiphoid comes from Greek xiphos, sword, and means shaped like a sword, as in the xiphoid process of the breastbone.

clue.text: Cockney artist, as it were, supporting diverse views

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual abbreviation for an artist
a true Cockney is born within the sound of Bow bells, so is someone in Bow

explanation.surface: A painter from London's East End backs a broad range of opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As it were' flags the loose reading: a Cockney artist is an RA IN BOW. Bow is a district of East London whose church bells define who counts as a Cockney.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainbow, as in rainbow coalition or flag, describes an alliance embracing many differing groups and outlooks.

clue.text: Sailing vessel having unknown crew from Hamburg

blocks.note: y is one of the algebraic unknowns
acht is German for eight, a rowing crew of eight

explanation.surface: A sailing boat takes on mystery crewmen from a German port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crew' means a rowing eight, and Hamburg makes it German.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht is a light boat with sails used for cruising or racing.

clue.text: Man giving up power in Darjeeling?

indicators.note: giving something up means letting it go, so a letter is dropped from the word for man

blocks.note: a chap is a man
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A ruler steps down from power in the Indian hill town of Darjeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: Darjeeling looks like the place, but with its question mark it is the tea; CHA is a British slang word for tea, from Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: Darjeeling is a variety of tea, and cha is an informal word for tea, so it is an example.

clue.text: Network disappointment for country squire?

blocks.note: LAN stands for local area network
a downer is something depressing or disappointing

explanation.surface: A broadband failure is a let-down for someone living in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A country squire is typically the chief owner of estates in a rural parish, so an example of a holder of property.

clue.text: Republican in sore need struggling back again

indicators.note: something struggling is in disarray, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Republican in great difficulty is once more fighting for support.
explanation.walkthrough: R stays at the front and the rest is a straight rearrangement of the two words, so all nine letters can be shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to support or back, so re-endorsing is giving that support a second time.

clue.text: "My cat foe a bobcat" - weird suggestion overruled by Sir David Attenborough?

definitions.text: suggestion overruled by Sir David Attenborough?

indicators.note: weird means strange and distorted, so the quoted phrase comes out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, all fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A nonsense line about a cat's enemy, oddly linked to the famous wildlife broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2016 an online public vote to name a British polar research ship chose this joke name; the government named the ship RRS Sir David Attenborough instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The joke name won the public poll but was set aside in favour of the broadcaster's name for the polar ship.

clue.text: Scandalous librarian's trial terminated early with support of a big star

indicators.note: ending something early cuts off its last part, so the final letter is lost
in a down answer support sits underneath, so the next pieces come below

blocks.note: a case is a trial in court
taken as written
a nova is a star that suddenly grows far brighter

explanation.surface: A disgraced librarian's court hearing is cut short, with backing from a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 's stands for 'is'. Casanova, the eighteenth-century Venetian seducer, spent his last years as librarian to Count Waldstein in Bohemia.
explanation.definitionFit: Casanova, infamous for his love affairs, worked as a librarian in a Bohemian castle in old age.

clue.text: Delivering global shifts in eye treatment?

blocks.note: a private eye is a detective, a tec for short
a tonic is a restorative medicine

explanation.surface: Eye drops might somehow be the cure that changes the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eye' suggests medicine for the eyes, but it is a private eye. The question mark flags this loose reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Tectonic describes movements of the plates of the earth's crust, which shift whole continents across the globe.

clue.text: A game of strategy in the past

blocks.note: taken as written
Go is the ancient East Asian board game of territory

explanation.surface: A strategic board game from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means before now, back in an earlier time, as in long ago.

clue.text: Distribution system spreads American article around capital of Zambia

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for spreads goes on either side of a letter
a capital is a first letter, so only the opening letter of Zambia is used

blocks.note: to lay is to spread out, as a table
its first letter
US is short for American
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A US aid scheme hands out goods around Lusaka, Zambia's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' tempts towards Lusaka, but it only means the first letter. LA(Z)YS + US + AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy Susan is a revolving tray on a dining table that passes dishes round to each diner.

clue.text: Year, end of year in Australia, seeing upturn in Louisiana pop music

indicators.note: in puts the preceding pieces inside the abbreviation for Australia
in a down answer turning something up reverses it, so the word for Australia reads backwards

blocks.note: Y is the abbreviation for year
December, abbreviated Dec, is the last month
Oz is the informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: As the year ends Down Under, Cajun dance music sees a boost in popularity.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the Australia piece is turned over; the year letters sit between its two letters once flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Zydeco is the accordion-led popular dance music of the Creole people of southwest Louisiana.

clue.text: United Church, in unhappy surroundings, may be displayed with relish

indicators.note: in, with surroundings, places the first two pieces inside the word for unhappy

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names
CE is the Church of England
unhappy is sad; surroundings shows it goes outside

explanation.surface: A church congregation in gloomy surroundings may yet show real enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with relish' reads as enthusiasm, but relish here is a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Food with relish has a tangy sauce or condiment added to it, so it is sauced.

clue.text: Fanatic stomaching disrespect - for their choice of clothing?

definitions.note: a cryptic hint, not a strict noun phrase

indicators.note: stomaching means taking into the belly, so the word for fanatic swallows the next piece

blocks.note: a nut is an enthusiast, as in fitness nut
dis is slang for disrespect

explanation.surface: An extremist puts up with insults because of how they dress.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the joke: this person's choice is to wear nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist chooses to go without clothes, so their choice of clothing is none at all.

clue.text: Boast supplied by Democratic supporters?

definitions.note: the answer is a singular collective noun for a group of supporters

blocks.note: to crow is to boast
D is the abbreviation for Democratic

explanation.surface: A political brag is put about by people on the Democratic side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporters' seems to belong with Democratic; it is the definition, while Democratic gives just D.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd is a mass of spectators, such as the fans at a match supporting a team.

clue.text: Live and perform for all to see amongst Arab people

blocks.note: to be is to exist or live
to do is to perform
U is the British film certificate for a universal audience
in means amongst

explanation.surface: Desert nomads live and put on a public show.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film classification meaning suitable for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bedouin are the nomadic Arab tribes of the deserts of Arabia and North Africa.

clue.text: See 7
Policeman heading off after doctor prescribes application for eye?

indicators.note: with its head gone, the policeman word loses its first letter
after places the shortened policeman behind the doctor

blocks.note: Dr is short for doctor
copper is slang for a policeman

explanation.surface: A policeman leaves after a doctor writes a prescription for eye drops.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: the answer is the device used to apply drops to an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A dropper is a small tube with a rubber bulb for putting medicine into the eye a drop at a time.

clue.text: One stops dog seizing line

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold, so the dog wraps around the next letter

blocks.note: a pug is a small flat-faced dog breed
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone halts a dog that has grabbed a lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug is a stopper that blocks a hole, such as in a basin, so it is something that stops.

clue.text: Look over playground and church

blocks.note: rec is British short for recreation ground, a public park
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a park and the church next to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Recce is British informal for reconnoitre, to survey or inspect an area before acting.

clue.text: Entrance to building vast at the front, see, and built badly

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept
something done badly is botched and disordered, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: its opening letter
taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The way into a building is huge at the front, and look, it has been poorly constructed.
